 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE  COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:15026  CRL.P No. 1483 of 2024  ORDER 1. Accused No.1 in Crime No.57/2023 registered by Kolar Women Police Station, Kolar, for the offences punishable under Sections 354(A), 506, 509, 34, 498A, 504, 376, 403, 306, 323, 344, 354,
357 and 405 of IPC, is before this Court under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

3. FIR in Crime No.57/2023 was registered by Kolar Women Police Station, Kolar, on 18.11.2023 against the petitioner and others for the aforesaid offences on the basis of private complaint filed by E V Ashalata before the Court of jurisdictional Magistrate which was referred to jurisdictional police by the learned Magistrate.
Apprehending arrest in the said case, petitioner had filed Crl.Misc.No.25/2024 before the Court of I Addl. Sessions Judge, Kolar, which was dismissed on 29.01.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition submits that allegations made in the complaint prima facie do not make out a case for the alleged offences.
Respondent No.2 is the wife of petitioner NC: 2024:KHC:15026 herein.
Petitioner has no criminal antecedents.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition.
6. The material on record would go to show that the relationship between respondent No.2 and petitioner herein who is her husband is strained.

Respondent No.2 has filed a private complaint before the Court of jurisdictional Magistrate which was referred to jurisdictional police by the learned Magistrate and in turn, FIR in Crime No.57/2023 is registered by Kolar Women Police Station, Kolar, against petitioner and others.
A perusal of the averments made in the complaint would go to show that the alleged offences under Sections 306 and 376 of IPC prima facie will not get attracted.

The police without appreciating this aspect of the matter, only for the reason that in the complaint, it is alleged that the aforesaid offences have been committed by accused have registered FIR for the offences as mentioned in the complaint.
Undisputedly, petitioner has no criminal antecedents.

Considering the relationship between the parties and also having regard to the Vijayachandra vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121301000/
2 nature of allegations made in the compliant, I am of the opinion NC: 2024:KHC:15026 that petitioner's prayer for grant of anticipatory bail is required to be answered affirmatively.

entities.text: Vijayachandra vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the following order:-
7.
The petition is allowed.

The respondent - Police or any other police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioner in the event of his arrest in Crime No.57/2023 registered by Kolar Women Police Station, Kolar, for the offences punishable under Sections 354(A), 506, 509, 34,
498A, 504, 376, 403, 306, 323, 344, 354, 357 and 405 of IPC, subject to the following conditions:
1. The Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of the copy of this order and shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the investigating officer.
2. Petitioner shall regularly appear before the Trial Court without fail unless exempted by the Trial Court for valid reasons.

3. Petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution witness and he shall co-operate with the police for investigation and appear before them whenever called upon.
NC: 2024:KHC:15026 4.

The petitioner shall not involve in similar offences in future;
Sd/-
